summary: Round 9, narrow re-check against the round-8 bytes (4cbbf960). Still prose only: no production logic, no wire change, and nothing in this diff adds, moves or authorises an object-store request. The M5.45f cell itself changed only status todo -> done with ADR-0044's summary; the three edits since round 8 are all in M5.66's cell and none of them breaks anything I passed at rounds 7 and 8. (1) The boundary pair is now two-sided -- at K = crossover exactly TWO requests and fewer bytes, at K = crossover + 1 exactly ONE request and exactly the whole-object bytes -- which closes the hole the pair existed to close ('at most two' is satisfied by the whole-object path at one) without disturbing criterion 2's independent bounds: the bounded path is still capped at two requests at every K, the header range plus one union slice, and the ~400 share still mandates exactly the whole-object GET. The two sides are consistent with the row's own direction of trade (bounded wins at low K, 2*objLen/(K+1) - 78,400 positive to K ~ 169), so crossover + 1 falling on the whole-object arm is the right side. (2) The dependency is now M5.45g AND M5.45h, and the new ground is verified against source rather than against the fix text: client/src/main/java/binjava/client/ holds exactly the five files the cell names (ConsumerClient, ConsumerRecord, DefaultEnvelope, Delivery, SubscriptionTransport), ConsumerClient.java:43-45 holds ONE RunKey per client, ConsumerClient.java:78 opens delivery.segment() with no byte source of its own, and backlog.md:69's M5.45h criterion 1 is 'a node holding K runs of one segment issues ONE fetch ... at K = 64' -- the mechanism, not merely an assertion. So the ground is right this time, and it is the cost-relevant one: without M5.45h's shared fetch, criterion 2's 'one union slice' at K = 169 and 'one request' at ~400 are dischargeable by a local driver reporting 2 and 1 where production issues 170 and 400, which is the runs-per-node scaling non-negotiable 6 forbids by name. The dependency chain is acyclic and every ID resolves: M5.66 -> M5.45g -> M5.45f (done), M5.66 -> M5.45h -> M5.45g and M5.62 (backlog.md:86, todo). (3) My round-8 minor is folded in the same cell: the cross-AZ arm is withdrawn rather than offered, 19,968 bytes per GET is named as R12's cross-AZ exchange rate, M5.9 is named as what makes the peer fetch unaddressable, time is stated as the only quantity left, the row now owes a latency derivation, and the K ~ 169 / K ~ 213 / K ~ 1,556 figures are explicitly inherited as byte-and-request counts rather than as a dollar crossover. The reconciliation of criteria 1 and 2 survives that withdrawal because the ~400 mandate rests on the physical argument -- SegmentWriter sorts runs by (indexId, partitionId), so a node's ~400 of 1,600 runs interleave and their union spans most of the 8 MiB -- not on the withdrawn price. Nothing remains. I did not re-derive the counted facts or the decisions verified at rounds 7 and 8, and I found nothing worth raising as a fresh minor.
